key_insight: The paper shows that discrete log-concavity of the ground state is a powerful structural property for proving when adiabatic quantum optimization can benefit from tunneling in convex potentials, even with a spike.
engineering_relevance: This provides a stronger theoretical basis for designing AQO Hamiltonians and estimating spectral gaps for a broader class of optimization landscapes than the classic Hamming-weight spike example.
method: Prove discrete log-concavity for ground states of a family of 1D discrete Schrödinger operators.
Use this structural result to derive new spectral gap bounds for convex potentials and some potentials with local minima.
Extend Reichardt-style perturbative tunneling analysis from linear to quadratic spike potentials.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical extensions and new spectral gap bounds, including a nontrivial quadratic potential case that is not exactly solvable.
watch_item: The results are theoretical and focused on 1D discrete models, so practical AQO performance on higher-dimensional or noisy hardware remains unverified.
paper_title: Log-concavity and tunneling: adiabatic quantum optimization for convex functions (with a spike)
